newsitem.title: USA: Fla. judge bars public access to smoking evidence.
newsitem.headline: Fla. judge bars public access to smoking evidence.

text.p: Full transcripts of depositions of tobacco chief executives and other evidence to be presented at next week's milestone secondhand-smoke trial will be kept from the public, a Florida judge has ruled.

The ruling also covers video recordings of depositions, or pre-trial questioning, and other exhibits to be introduced during trial, Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye said in a one-page order released on Tuesday but signed last week.

Kaye acted after lawyers pressing the secondhand smoke suit on behalf of some 60,000 nonsmoking flight attendants released to some reporters written and videotaped excerpts of pre-trial questioning of tobacco company industry CEO's.

The class-action suit going to trial next week in Dade County Court alleges that tobacco companies knew but hid the dangers of smoking and cigarettes for decades. It is the first trial of a secondhand smoke lawsuit, and the plaintiff lawyers have said they will seek $5 billion or more in damages.

Kaye wrote he was ordering the court's clerk to keep the transcripts and other exhibits from reporters and the public "in order to preserve the integrity of the trial and the sanctity of the testimony of the witnesses."

Neither side in the six-year-old case has detailed what evidence would be presented at the trial but the lawyers have dueled in hearings over the possible use of industry documents, including those handed over by Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett to state attorneys general in settling a lawsuit.

A reporter from The Miami Herald newspaper said last week in court the newspaper objected to limiting access to trial evidence but an attorney for the newspaper was not immediately available for comment on Kaye's order.
